summary: Best-available on pools without the orphan rule (decouple the ordering projection)
description:
### Best-available on pools that do not want the orphan rule

**As** an organizer whose venue has the orphan-prevention rule OFF, **I want** best-available
seat selection to work on my performances, **so that** a product decision about stranded seats
does not silently decide whether buyers can ask for "4 together".

TKT-81 shipped best-available reading the ordering projection (`row_key`, `row_rank`,
`position` on `seat_claim_adjacency`). That projection is written only when
`orphan_prevention_enabled` is on, because ADR-041 provisioned it for the orphan rule and
TKT-81 deliberately did not decouple the two — decoupling changes what catalog emits and what
`ProvisionSeated` requires, which ADR-041's own delivery section shows is an ordered,
multi-ticket, three-service rollout. Bundling it into a ticket about selection would have
joined two independent risks.

The consequence is real and currently visible only as a refusal: such a pool answers
`best_available_unsupported`, deterministically, for every party size, until it is
re-provisioned. That code exists precisely so the limitation is legible rather than presenting
as a sellout — see ADR-061 § Consequences, which names this as the follow-up it most expects to
be superseded by.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] A seated performance whose bound map has orphan prevention OFF still receives an ordering
      projection at provisioning, and best-available works on it.
- [ ] The orphan rule remains OFF on those pools — the projection and the rule are independent,
      and turning one on must not turn the other on. Proven by a pool that serves best-available
      and still permits a stranding named-seat selection.
- [ ] Existing rule-off seated pools are repaired by the correction-wave path, not by a
      migration, following ADR-041's ordering and TKT-81's rank-only-correction rule.
- [ ] `best_available_unsupported` remains reachable for a pool that genuinely has no projection
      — the state must stay distinguishable rather than becoming unreachable and untested.

**Depends on:** TKT-81 (Done). Governing: ADR-041 (rollout ordering, consumer-before-producer),
ADR-061 (what the projection carries and why the rank is correctable), ADR-017 (any schema bump).

**Quality gates (every story):**
- `make check` green
- Contract tests pass for any touched service boundary (ADR-009 drift check)

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Blocker cleared (TKT-81 is Done) — needs shaping before Gate 1

Backlog review 2026-08-25 at HEAD `ad849f98`.

**Removed the stale `blocked-by: TKT-81`.** Best-available shipped in TKT-81, which is what this ticket builds on rather than waits for — it is the origin, not a dependency. A stale blocker matters here because the board hard-blocks the Gate 1 drag on an open blocker.

**The gap is confirmed at HEAD, not inherited.** `services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go:169-174` still short-circuits: `if !in.orphanPrevention { return in, nil }`. A pool whose organizer has the orphan rule **off** never gets the geometry fetch, so `seat_claim_adjacency` carries no `row_key` / `row_rank` / `position`, so best-available has nothing to order by and answers `best_available_unsupported` (`api/server.go:439`) forever.

**The ticket's framing is right and worth preserving:** a *product* decision about stranded seats currently decides, silently, whether a buyer can ask for "4 together" at all. Those are two different questions and one is answering the other.

**Not shaped yet** — no `readiness` object. It needs the 8-item DoR before Gate 1. Two things shaping should establish, both cheap to read: what catalog must emit when the rule is off (the decoupling changes the event payload, so **ADR-017** governs — bump on consumer semantics), and what `ProvisionSeated` then requires. Recommend **not** `risk:low`: it changes a domain event's payload and an ADR (ADR-041) provisioned the projection for the orphan rule specifically.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Re-verified at HEAD — still unshaped, and the gap is confirmed

Backlog review 2026-08-26 at HEAD `1aaee7cd`, one day after the blocker was cleared.

The short-circuit is still live: `services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go:169-174` — `if !in.orphanPrevention { return in, nil }`. A pool whose organizer has the orphan rule **off** never gets the geometry fetch, so `seat_claim_adjacency` carries no `row_key`/`row_rank`/`position` and best-available answers `best_available_unsupported` forever (`api/server.go:439`).

**Still needs the 8-item DoR.** Two things shaping must establish, both cheap to read and both named yesterday:
- What catalog must emit when the rule is off. The decoupling changes the event payload, so **ADR-017 governs** — bump on consumer semantics, not parse compatibility, and the consumer must dispatch on `schema` before decoding `data`.
- The correction-wave path for existing rule-off seated pools, since the AC says repair by that path and **not** by a migration.

**Not a product decision** — the product question ("should stranded seats be prevented?") is already answered per-organizer; this ticket's whole point is that the answer is wrongly deciding a second, unrelated question. That framing is right and worth preserving.

**Sizing caution:** ADR-041's own delivery section shows this as an ordered, multi-ticket, three-service rollout. Shaping should expect to slice it rather than plan it whole.
